attempt: Not reproduced under these conditions. Original attempt: the authors' Makefile as documented (make Res1) cannot run because the archive has no makefile.inc (the Makefile includes it and it names the compiler and the BLAS/LAPACK objects); the log is kept. Build-only patch: a makefile.inc written from the Makefile's own variable names with gfortran (conda-forge), -O2 -std=legacy, the bundled lapack.f and dblas.f compiled as objects, and one prerequisite line for driver. No source file was edited; verify_sources records build-only (compared 6 archive source files, none modified). Pass 1 (recorded -O2 build, make Res1) and pass 2 (clean directory, same binary) both give 0.565126294872521D-01. Pass 2 in a different environment (a separate tree compiled at -O0, same sources; the only environment change is the optimisation level, so this confirmation is weak) gives the same value. |ours - shipped| = 3.2e-10 against the registered tolerance 1e-12. Across the whole output (724 numbers) 712 differ by more than 1e-12, the largest by 6.4e-8, so this is a systematic difference in the spline values, not a print-rounding effect. Compiler optimisation level is ruled out as the cause (-O0 and -O2 identical). The cause is not localised. The untested hypothesis is that the authors' build used an external LAPACK/BLAS (the Makefile's LAPACK and BLAS variables suggest it) rather than the bundled lapack.f and dblas.f; the next experiment is to link against a conda-forge BLAS/LAPACK and see whether the values move toward the shipped ones. Until then this is a not-reproduced verdict under these conditions, not a claim about the paper's method.
